branch_hypotheses.divergence_signal: Public messaging shifts from whether to retire to what conditions and timeline govern retirement.
branch_hypotheses.plausible_path: Board recommends early retirement bundled with worker transition package and replacement resource sequencing.
branch_hypotheses.trigger: Board receives a reliability pathway showing manageable replacement risk and regulator signals cost recovery openness if conditions are met.

branch_hypotheses.divergence_signal: Board and management repeatedly foreground reserve margins, contingency planning, and timing uncertainty.
branch_hypotheses.plausible_path: Board recommends delayed retirement or staged operation while seeking more planning and procurement.
branch_hypotheses.trigger: Reliability memo emphasizes near-term adequacy risk without fast replacement options.

branch_hypotheses.divergence_signal: Comment volume becomes dominated by rates language rather than emissions or labor fairness.
branch_hypotheses.plausible_path: Member-owner opposition grows, reducing board appetite for aggressive retirement despite climate pressure.
branch_hypotheses.trigger: Cost recovery appears likely to raise bills materially or is framed that way in member discourse.

branch_hypotheses.divergence_signal: Regulatory and board documents begin naming labor protections as explicit predicates for retirement.
branch_hypotheses.plausible_path: Retirement remains possible, but only through a negotiated package with severance, retraining, transfer rights, or phased closure.
branch_hypotheses.trigger: Union credibly threatens procedural opposition unless transition terms are concrete and enforceable.

branch_hypotheses.divergence_signal: Management begins emphasizing balance-sheet exposure and legal uncertainty over climate commitments.
branch_hypotheses.plausible_path: Board defers or narrows retirement recommendation because implementation without cost recovery becomes financially unattractive.
branch_hypotheses.trigger: Regulator letter or later filings question prudence of stranded cost recovery.

risk_flags.description: Corpus is concise and provides scenario scaffolding rather than detailed facts, so several counts and weight calibrations are inferred defaults.
Decision authority is clearly divided between board recommendation, regulator cost recovery approval, and worker negotiation leverage.
No explicit stranded cost magnitude, rate impact, or replacement cost estimates are provided, limiting precision on elasticity and backlash risk.
Two non-actor placeholders were removed conceptually but remain as zero-weight edges due to strict shape preservation risk; later cleanup may be needed for simulation integrity.
Hearings, letters, and studies are likely along the path; they should not be mistaken for terminal outcomes unless they satisfy endpoint criteria.

source_evidence: fictional regional energy cooperative must decide whether to retire an old gas plant early

simulation_brief.summary: A fictional regional energy cooperative is weighing early retirement of an aging gas plant amid member-owner concern, grid reliability analysis, climate advocacy pressure, labor transition demands, and state regulatory oversight. The board can recommend retirement timing, the state regulator can approve or constrain cost recovery, and workers can negotiate transition terms that affect feasibility and coalition stability.
simulation_brief.t0_posture: pre-decision with active public pressure and unresolved operational constraints
simulation_brief.title: regional_energy_cooperative_gas_plant_retirement_decision
uncertainty_notes: No detailed plant economics, worker counts, or exact service territory population are provided.
The scenario implies but does not quantify reliability risk, political salience, and cost recovery exposure.
Member-owner opinion is present but not numerically specified; represented as split cohorts rather than a single majority.

sociology_baseline.evidence: members likely respond more to frames close to existing concerns like rates, reliability, and fairness than to abstract claims
many members likely remain passive until visible rate, reliability, or fairness cues cross a threshold

local economic ties and advocacy networks likely reinforce within-group narratives
support for a consequential infrastructure shift likely needs repeated signals from trusted institutions and peers
worker, community, and owner identities shape interpretation of the same facts
unless punctuated by hearings, letters, or bill impacts, broader member attention may drift

sociology_prompt_influences.description: Technical reliability claims can legitimize delay or conditional retirement if repeated by trusted internal experts.
Worker protection language can bridge climate and labor camps if made concrete and enforceable.
Cost recovery framing strongly affects whether members and regulator view retirement as prudent or burdensome.
Board recommendation precedes or shapes regulatory cost recovery review, which in turn conditions practical implementation.
